description: FLAMEWISE is a team of ambitious engineers determined to lead and win. We developed an interactive, data-driven dashboard from NASA’s PSI investigations. Powered by curiosity and cutting-edge engineering, we turn complex science into life saving solutions for deep space exploration.
summary: FLAMEWISE turns decades of NASA microgravity-combustion research into one interactive, AI-powered experience instead of scattered reports. Users fly the FLAMEWISE-1 spacecraft in 3D using hand gestures or a mouse. In the Combustion Lab, they set oxygen, fuel and gravity and watch a 3D flame change live: a teardrop on Earth, a sphere in orbit. A side-by-side 1 g vs 0 g view and a Density X-Ray show why. A physics model calibrated on NASA FLEX results computes oxygen limits, flame temperature and burn time, while a machine-learning model predicts extinction. The Safety & Security System adds a live station map with airflow and smoke, infrared cameras that detect invisible cool and alcohol flames, FireNet risk prediction, alarms and crew protocols. Its NASA knowledge assistant retrieves, ranks and cites findings from 14 experiments, including FLEX, BASS, Saffire, SoFIE, Apollo 1 and Mir. Mark-L, a voice AI assistant, explains what users see, and cinematic Apollo 1 and Apollo 13 stories connect the lessons to history. Every result is labeled as NASA data, simulation or AI prediction. This matters because crews heading to the Moon and Mars need fire-safety knowledge that is easy to find, compare and understand.
details:
What it does and how it works
FLAMEWISE turns decades of NASA microgravity-combustion research into one interactive, AI-powered experience. Instead of searching through scattered reports, users explore the findings inside a cinematic 3D mission. They start in a galaxy intro, board the FLAMEWISE-1 spacecraft and travel between Earth, the Moon and Mars using hand gestures or a mouse. A generator fire emergency starts the investigation.

  • Combustion Lab: users set oxygen level, fuel type, droplet size and gravity, and a transparent 3D flame changes live. It is a flickering teardrop on Earth and a sphere fed only by diffusion in orbit. A side-by-side 1 g vs 0 g comparison and a Density X-Ray view show why. A physics model calibrated on NASA FLEX results computes oxygen limits, flame temperature and burn time, and a machine-learning model predicts extinction probability.
  • Safety & Security System: a station-wide fire-safety deck with a live three-floor station map with airflow and smoke, and zone controls with a flame simulation. Six infrared cameras (0.4–14 µm) reveal invisible alcohol flames and cool flames. It also includes oxygen, ventilation and reactor controls, FireNet (a neural network that predicts ignition risk), alarms and NASA-based crew protocols. Its knowledge assistant retrieves, ranks and cites findings from 14 experiments (FLEX, BASS, Saffire, SoFIE, SAME, ACME, Apollo 1, Mir) and refuses to answer when evidence is weak.
  • Mark-L AI assistant: a voice assistant that sees the user’s current settings, explains them, and runs the FLAMEWISE physics and ML models on request.
  • Apollo 1 & Apollo 13 stories: cinematic, respectful retellings based only on NASA-verified facts, connecting today’s fire-safety rules to their history.

Benefits and intended impact
FLAMEWISE makes NASA’s fire research easy to find, compare and understand. It shows students, the public and future engineers how gravity, oxygen and ventilation change fire risk, which matters as crews return to the Moon and head to Mars. We hope it inspires young people in Oman and the region to pursue space science, engineering and AI.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • Languages: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML/CSS, GLSL.
  • 3D: a custom WebGL2 engine with ray-marched volumetric flames.
  • Safety system: React and Tailwind CSS.
  • AI and ML: scikit-learn Random Forests; PyTorch (FireNet, trained on 24,000 simulated runs based on FLEX, Saffire and BASS findings); hybrid retrieval (BM25 + rank fusion); Google Gemini; Mark-L by FatihMakes (CC BY-NC 4.0); MediaPipe hand tracking.
  • Data and charts: NumPy, pandas, matplotlib.
  • Testing: Playwright automated browser tests.
  • Hardware: a standard laptop with a webcam, microphone and speakers.

Creativity
FLAMEWISE combines a game-like space mission, real combustion physics, machine learning, infrared vision and a voice AI assistant in one story. Users control a spacecraft with their hands, “x-ray” a flame and see fires that the human eye cannot.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: every result is labeled as NASA data, published finding, simulation or ML prediction, and the ML models are clearly marked as trained on synthetic data.
  • Primary sources: NASA FLEX, BASS, Saffire, the Combustion Science program, the ISS Researcher’s Guide and NASA’s Apollo records.
  • Respect: the Apollo stories are non-graphic and contain no invented dialogue.
  • Security: API keys stay on the local server and are never sent to the browser.
  • Accessibility: mouse, keyboard or hand gestures, captions, and an ordinary laptop with no special hardware.
  • Licensing: open-source components are credited, and the project is for non-commercial use.
